extracted.intended_audience: neuroscientists, neuroesthetics researchers, and cognitive neuroscientists planning fMRI studies of aesthetic experience (particularly mathematical beauty)
extracted.subtask_description: Designing, conducting, analyzing, and reporting an fMRI experiment that links subjective aesthetic ratings of mathematical formulae to brain activity, with explicit procedures for stimuli, participant selection, behavioral measures, scanning, and statistical analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participant selection and eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Recruit subjects with appropriate expertise (here: 16 mathematicians at postgraduate or postdoctoral level; normal or corrected-to-normal vision; note left/right handedness), exclude participants with confounding medication/conditions (one excluded for ADHD medication).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select domain-expert participants when stimuli require advanced knowledge; screen for neuropsychiatric/medication confounds; report demographics (age, sex, handedness) and sample size; discuss limits of generalizability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics and consent
rubrics_metrics.description: Obtain written informed consent and institutional ethics committee approval prior to study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report ethics committee name, consent procedure, and any exclusions arising from ethical/safety screening.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of control (non-expert) group with limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Recruit non-mathematician subjects to gauge baseline reactions, but acknowledge limitations because many 'non-mathematicians' may have some mathematical training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use control data cautiously; document understanding levels in controls; interpret beauty judgments by non-experts as possibly formal (visual) reactions rather than cognitive understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stimulus set size and selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a defined stimulus set (here: 60 mathematical formulae) chosen to span a range of aesthetic judgments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a complete list of stimuli (supplementary materials) and rationale for inclusion; ensure variety across complexity, familiarity, and subfields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-scan beauty rating scale and procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Have subjects study the full stimulus set before scanning and rate each item on a detailed beauty scale (here: −5 'ugly' to +5 'beautiful') several weeks before scanning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use pre-scan ratings to characterize and balance stimuli per subject; provide raw pre-scan data as supplementary material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scan-time beauty rating categories and coding
rubrics_metrics.description: During scanning, obtain in-scan categorical beauty ratings (here: Ugly / Neutral / Beautiful), encoded numerically (−1, 0, +1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use an abridged in-scan scale suitable for response devices and timing constraints; report coding explicitly so it can be modeled as parametric or categorical regressor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-scan understanding (comprehension) rating
rubrics_metrics.description: After scanning, ask subjects to rate their level of understanding of each stimulus on a numeric scale (here: 0 'no understanding' to 3 'profound understanding').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect understanding ratings to dissociate cognitive comprehension from aesthetic experience; make these ratings available in supplementary data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of pre-scan ratings to balance stimulus sequence
rubrics_metrics.description: Partition stimuli into groups (here: 20 low, 20 medium, 20 high pre-scan beauty ratings per subject) and use these to construct scanning sessions so each session contains equal numbers from each group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance sequences individually per subject to avoid bias and to distribute preferred/non-preferred stimuli across sessions; document grouping algorithm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pseudo-randomization constraints (avoid consecutive same-category)
rubrics_metrics.description: Organize the pseudo-randomized sequence so that no two consecutively presented equations are from the same pre-scan rating group (low/medium/high).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Impose sequence constraints to avoid run-length confounds; report the randomization method and checks (e.g., counts per session).

rubrics_metrics.name: Trial timing and session structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Define trial timing precisely: here each equation displayed 16 s, followed by 1 s blank, 3 s response window, then 1–2 s inter-trial interval; sessions start with a 19.5 s blank (T1 equilibration) and end with a 30 s blank; 15 trials per session, 4 sessions total.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose timings that allow adequate stimulus exposure and baseline collection; report all temporal parameters so analyses (e.g., boxcar modeling, HRF convolution) are reproducible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stimulus presentation hardware and software specifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Report presentation software and hardware (here: Cogent 2000; Epson projector 1600×1200, 60 Hz; back-projection onto translucent screen viewed via mirror).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include display resolution, refresh rate, viewing geometry, and response device; provide details enabling replication of visual angles and luminance conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visual appearance parameters
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify visual presentation characteristics (here: font color in CIE 1931 XYZ: 755,761,637; gray background CIE: 236,228,200; overall brightness 280–324 cd/m^2; equation width 4°–24° visual angle; height 1°–5°).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report color coordinates, luminance, and visual angle ranges to control low-level visual confounds and to interpret visual cortex activations.

rubrics_metrics.name: fMRI acquisition parameters
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide scanner and sequence parameters: e.g., 3-T Siemens Magnetom Trio with 32-channel head coil; B0 fieldmap acquired; EPI for BOLD (TE=30 ms, TR/volume time described, 48 axial slices 2 mm thick with 1 mm gap, voxel resolution 3×3×3 mm); high-resolution anatomical T1 MDEFT (176 slices, 1 mm isotropic).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report all acquisition details needed for preprocessing and localization (scanner, coil, TE, TR, slice prescription, slice thickness/gap, voxel size, fieldmap and anatomical sequence parameters).

rubrics_metrics.name: Preprocessing and analysis software
rubrics_metrics.description: Use established analysis packages (here: SPM8) and cite relevant methodological references (e.g., Friston et al., 2006).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State preprocessing steps (realignment, normalization, smoothing) and software versions; reference methodological choices and rationale; supply scripts where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modeling with parametric modulators
rubrics_metrics.description: Model trial events with parametric modulators for understanding and scan-time beauty (beauty coded −1/0/1; understanding 0–3), entered as first- and second-level parametric modulators respectively to separate variance components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use orthogonalization carefully (SPM orthogonalization) to ensure one modulator captures variance not explained by the other; report ordering and coding of modulators explicitly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Orthogonalization to dissociate correlated regressors
rubrics_metrics.description: Exploit SPM orthogonalization so that the beauty modulator captures variance unexplained by understanding (and vice versa in the alternate model), allowing isolation of 'beauty only' and 'understanding only' effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain limitations: orthogonalization partitions variance but a common portion remains un-attributable; consider alternate analyses (e.g., separate models) to verify findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parametric vs categorical analysis distinction
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer parametric analyses when modeling graded relationships (sensitivity to rated quantity), and use categorical analyses to obtain averaged parameter estimates for discrete categories; recognize parametric analyses are often more sensitive and allow orthogonalization approaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report both analyses when informative; clarify the different interpretations and sensitivity trade-offs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Second-level (group) random effects analysis and contrasts
rubrics_metrics.description: Take single-subject contrast images to second-level random effects analyses (one-sample t-tests) for population inference, and perform contrasts such as parametric beauty, categorical beauty, and All equations vs Baseline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use appropriate random-effects models for group inference; report df and test statistics; consider conjunction analyses for overlap questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conjunction-null analysis for overlap testing
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a conjunction-null analysis (Nichols et al., 2005) to test overlap between contrasts (e.g., parametric beauty activation and de-activation maps).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify thresholding applied to each contrast prior to conjunction; cite the conjunction method and discuss interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical thresholding and multiple comparisons correction
rubrics_metrics.description: Define cluster- and peak-level significance criteria and correction methods: here report cluster-level significance P_Clust-FWE < 0.05 with background threshold P_unc < 0.001 and extent threshold 10 voxels; for other contrasts report peak-voxel P_FWE < 0.05.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State exact thresholds, correction method (FWE), and extent thresholds; provide both cluster- and peak-level results, and be transparent about uncorrected findings labeled as exploratory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate space and localization reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Report activation coordinates in a standard stereotactic space (here: MNI) and provide anatomical labels and Brodmann area references where possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give cluster sizes (voxels), peak T and P values, and coordinates; include tables of activations and de-activations and show images with crosshairs for hotspots.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling imbalanced or missing category counts
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge that uneven counts across categories (e.g., fewer 'Ugly' ratings) reduce estimation efficiency but do not bias inference; report sessions where categories are missing and discuss impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design analyses robust to imbalance (e.g., parametric modulators) and report how imbalance affects sensitivity; avoid claiming absence of effect solely due to imbalance without power considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting non-significant activations transparently
rubrics_metrics.description: Document activations that do not reach significance as potentially interesting and leave them to future studies to ascertain their roles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List subthreshold clusters (with coordinates and peak statistics) but distinguish them clearly from statistically significant findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide full behavioral and supplementary materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Supply raw behavioral data and experimental materials as supplementary Data Sheets (e.g., EquationsForm.pdf, UnderstandingForm.pdf, BehavioralData.xlsx, BeauNeutUglyBase.pdf).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make questionnaires, rating scales, and data tables available to enable replication, reanalysis, and transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use post-scan subjective questionnaires to corroborate emotional reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect qualitative and quantitative post-scan responses about emotional reactions, pleasure, and heightened states of consciousness to link subjective reports with neural correlates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report distribution of subjective responses and integrate them in interpretation; use them to support claims about 'aesthetic emotion' when correlated with neural data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretive caution regarding causality and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Be cautious in interpretation (e.g., mOFC activity correlates parametrically with beauty ratings after accounting for understanding) and discuss alternative explanations and limitations (sample size, expertise requirement, cultural factors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss whether findings generalize beyond expert subjects and particular stimuli; suggest future work to test broader populations and stimulus types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of domain-specific confounds (visual vs cognitive sources of beauty)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether aesthetic responses arise from formal/visual features versus cognitive understanding (e.g., less-understood equations elicit stronger visual cortex activity suggesting formal/form-based aesthetics).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Model understanding and beauty jointly; interpret visual-area activations as potential indicators of form-driven aesthetic response, and design follow-ups to isolate form from content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory reporting items: funding, conflicts, and acknowledgments
rubrics_metrics.description: Declare funding sources (e.g., Wellcome Trust award), conflicts of interest (none here), and acknowledge contributions (e.g., methodological suggestions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include these declarations as standard reporting practice to ensure transparency and to identify potential sources of bias.
